user.title: Connect to Crowdergy
user.description: Sign in with your Crowdergy account. Create one in the Crowdergy app first.

data_description.email: Email address of your Crowdergy account.

location.title: Location
location.description: Tell us where your devices live. Used for aggregation — pre-filled from your HA coordinates.

data_description.entity_outdoor_temp_c: Sensor with the current outdoor temperature in °C — shown in the app header. Leave empty and Crowdergy fetches the value automatically from Open-Meteo (weather data for your district).

device_type.title: Device #{device_number} — type & name
device_type.description: Pick the device type and a name. In the next step you'll link the related Home Assistant entities.

data_description.device_type: Determines which entities are requested in the next step.
data_description.device_name: Display name in the Crowdergy app and in Home Assistant.

device_entities.title: {device_name} ({device_type}) — link entities
device_entities.description: Link the Home Assistant entities relevant for this device type. All fields are optional; missing values are ignored.

data_description.entity_current_power_kw: Sensor providing current power in W or kW.
data_description.read_section: These entities are only read by Crowdergy.
data_description.control_section: Crowdergy controls the device by writing one of two values to the entity below — "device on" → value_on, "device off" → value_off.

read_section.name: Power data (read-only)
read_section.description: These entities are only read by Crowdergy.

data.entity_energy_discharged_total: Out-flow energy entity (kWh, cumulative) — battery / grid

data_description.entity_current_power_kw: Sensor providing current power in W or kW.
data_description.entity_soc_percent: Sensor providing current state of charge in percent.
data_description.entity_vehicle_status: Sensor or binary-sensor entity for vehicle status (e.g. "connected", "charging").
data_description.entity_current_temp_c: Current temperature in °C — e.g. flow temperature of a heat pump or the inside temperature of a DHW tank. Shown next to the heat-pump tile in the app.
data_description.entity_target_temp_c: Current target / setpoint temperature in °C. Optional — when empty the app only shows the current temperature. Crowdergy does NOT write this entity; you keep controlling the setpoint via your HA heating integration. Crowdergy reads the value to plan heating windows.
data_description.entity_energy_total: Sensor with state_class total_increasing in kWh (lifetime counter). Crowdergy computes daily/monthly/yearly consumption via delta math. Optional — without this sensor the app keeps showing kW only.
data_description.entity_energy_discharged_total: Optional second total_increasing kWh counter for the OTHER direction. Battery: discharge counter (`energy_total` above carries the charge counter). Grid: export counter (`energy_total` carries the import counter). When both are mapped Crowdergy stores the net signed value so the chart shows one bar per slot (consumption / import vs export / discharge). Leave empty if your inverter only exposes one signed sensor — that single value is used as-is.

control_section.name: Control (Crowdergize)
control_section.description: Which HA entities may Crowdergy control? Wallbox: a charge-mode select for the app picker AND optionally a control entity for later smart on/off logic. Other types: just the control entity + "on"/"off" values in the next step.

data_description.entity_control: Any writable HA entity: switch, number, select, input helper, climate, light, fan. Toggled automatically by Crowdergy whenever Crowdergize is on (smart logic comes later).
data_description.entity_charge_mode: Select entity offering the app's charge modes (e.g. "Power Mode" / "Lock Mode" / "Solar Pure Mode") as options.

device_values.title: {device_name} ({device_type}) — control values
device_values.description: Which values should Crowdergy write to "{entity_control}" when the device turns on or off? For select/number/climate entities the picker is filled automatically.

add_more.title: Add another device?
add_more.description: You can add more devices or finish setup.
